title: Active and Passive Verbs
summary: How to recognise a passive verb, how to change active sentences into passive ones (and back), the passive forms Checkpoint asks about and why writers use the passive.

blocks.text: In an **active** sentence, the subject **does** the action. In a **passive** sentence, the subject **receives** the action, and the doer moves to the end after **by**, or disappears.

items: **Active:** *The children **painted** the wall.* (the children do the action)
**Passive:** *The wall **was painted** by the children.* (the wall receives the action)
**Passive with no doer:** *The wall **was painted** last week.*

blocks.title: How to recognise a passive verb
blocks.text: Look for a form of **be** + a **past participle**: *is made, was found, were taken, has been opened, have been sold, will be built.* If there is no *be* before the past participle, it is not passive.

items: Take the **object** of the active sentence and make it the **subject**.
Add the correct form of **be**, in the **same tense** as the active verb.
Add the **past participle** of the main verb.
Add **by + the doer** only if it is important.

blocks.text: Notice that the verb **be** must agree with the new subject: *fifty trees **were** planted* (plural), *one tree **was** planted* (singular).

rows: The council **has opened** a new park.
A new park **has been opened** (by the council).

blocks.title: The two forms most often asked about
items: **Simple past passive** = **was / were + past participle**: *was found, were taken, was built, were invited*.
**Present perfect passive** = **has / have + been + past participle**: *has been found, have been taken, has been built*.
To tell them apart, look for **been**. If you see *has been / have been* + past participle, it is present perfect passive.

blocks.text: Find the doer (after **by**), make it the subject, and put the verb in the same tense without *be*.

items: *The cake **was eaten** by the twins.* → *The twins **ate** the cake.*
*The match **has been won** by our team.* → *Our team **has won** the match.*
If there is no doer, choose a sensible one: *My bag **was taken**.* → *Someone **took** my bag.*

blocks.text: 5. Why do writers use the passive?
This is a favourite reading question. Learn these answers:

items: to focus on the **thing** or the **action**, not on who did it (*The pyramids were built over 4,000 years ago.*)
because the doer is **unknown** (*My phone was stolen.*)
because the doer is **obvious** or **not important** (*The thief was arrested.* We know it was the police.)
to make the writing sound **formal** and **factual**, as in reports, news reports and science texts
in stories: to hide who did something, which creates **mystery** (*The window had been smashed.*)

blocks.title: Watch out for these
items: Missing *be*: *The bike stolen yesterday* ✗ → *The bike **was** stolen yesterday* ✓
Wrong participle: *The vase was broke* ✗ → *The vase was **broken*** ✓
Wrong agreement: *The windows was cleaned* ✗ → *The windows **were** cleaned* ✓
Wrong tense of *be*: *Active: They built it in 1990.* → *It **is** built in 1990* ✗ → *It **was** built in 1990* ✓
Not every *was* + word is passive: *She was tired* is not passive (*tired* is an adjective here, there is no action done to her).

blocks.title: Reading questions in this style
items: *Tick one box to show the verb form of the highlighted verb.* (for example: simple past passive / present perfect passive)
*Find and copy a passive verb from the paragraph.*
*Why does the writer use the passive in this sentence?* (focus on the action, doer unknown or not important, formal tone, mystery)

blocks.title: Worked example (tick-one style)
blocks.text: *Text: ...the old lighthouse **has been repaired** and will open again in June.* Which verb form is the highlighted verb? **A** simple past passive **B** present perfect passive **C** present progressive **D** past perfect. **Answer: B**, because it is *has been* + the past participle *repaired*.

**In your writing**, a few passive sentences show a range of verb forms (Grammar and punctuation) and make non-fiction sound formal (Vocabulary and language). Use it where it fits, not in every sentence.

items: News report: *Two children **were rescued** from the sea on Friday afternoon.*
Information text: *Papyrus **was made** from a plant that grows beside the Nile.*
Formal letter: *I **was told** that the library would be closed for a month.*
Mystery story: *The drawer **had been opened**, and the map was gone.*

blocks.title: نصيحة سريعة
items: المبني للمجهول = فعل be + التصريف الثالث. لو مفيش be يبقى مش passive.
لو لقيت been بعد has أو have يبقى present perfect passive. لو was أو were بس يبقى simple past passive.
لما يسألك ليه الكاتب استخدم passive: يا إما الفاعل مش معروف، يا إما مش مهم، يا إما عشان الكلام يبقى رسمي، أو عشان يعمل غموض في القصة.

items.q: Active or passive? *The letter was delivered this morning.*
Which verb form is it? *Three new classrooms have been built.*
Which verb form is it? *The winners were chosen by the judges.*
Change to passive: *A strong wind knocked down the tree.*
items.a: *The tree was knocked down by a strong wind.*

items.q: Change to passive (no doer needed): *Someone has broken the window.*
Why does a news report say *A man has been rescued from the river* and not name the rescuers?
items.a: The passive focuses on the man and the rescue, which is the important news; it also sounds formal and factual.

items.q: Change to active: *The museum was visited by two hundred pupils.*
Correct the mistake: *The new shops was opened last week.*
items.a: *The new shops **were** opened last week.* (*shops* is plural)

items.q: Change to passive: *They will serve lunch at one o'clock.*
items.a: *Lunch will be served at one o'clock.*

items.q: Is this sentence passive? *The sky was very dark.* Explain.
items.a: **No.** *dark* is an adjective, not a past participle, and nothing is being done to the sky.
